intro: Look for the portal. Here in Konya province, the Slender Minaret Madrasa, a madrasa and hospital from 1265, carries the boldest piece of Seljuk carving: an inscription knotted across the stone like ribbon. Today the building is a museum of stone and wood.
history: The madrasa was built at Konya in 1265 for the vizier Sahip Ata. Its portal, where the inscription is knotted across the stone like ribbon, is the boldest piece of Seljuk carving. The slender minaret that gave the building its name lost its upper part to lightning in 1901. Today the madrasa lives on as a museum of stone and wood.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the portal and the slender minaret. Then step into the domed courtyard and take your time with the stone collection.
facts: Did you know? Its courtyard is domed rather than open, and very few Anatolian madrasas were built closed like this. On its portal, the inscription is knotted across the stone like ribbon — the boldest piece of Seljuk carving. And the slender minaret that gave the building its name lost its upper part to lightning in 1901.
outro: This brings our visit to the Slender Minaret Madrasa to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let this carved stone keep speaking to those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
